name: Services Directive
evidence_rating: thin: model-based estimates of the effect of the barriers removed; no causal ex-post study found
summary: The Directive required Member States to remove unjustified barriers to establishing and providing services and to set up points of single contact. A Commission economists' assessment (2012) estimated gains in trade, investment and GDP from the barriers actually removed, but its authors describe it as an extrapolation rather than a full ex-post evaluation; a 2015 review by Sweden's National Board of Trade found no ex-post analysis of the Directive's effects.

indicators.objective: No monitoring indicators set in the proposal; assessed through the Commission's reports listed below

literature.citation: Monteagudo, J., Rutkowski, A. and Lorenzani, D. (2012), The economic impact of the Services Directive: a first assessment following implementation, European Economy Economic Papers 456, European Commission (DG ECFIN)
literature.authors: Monteagudo, J., Rutkowski, A. and Lorenzani, D.
literature.title: The economic impact of the Services Directive: a first assessment following implementation
literature.venue: European Economy Economic Papers 456, European Commission (DG ECFIN)
literature.method: quantitative assessment (barrier indicators before and after implementation, gravity-model estimates)
literature.headline: Estimates gains in intra-EU services trade, FDI and GDP from the barriers removed by implementation; authors describe it as an updated prediction rather than an assessment of full effects
literature.summary_plain: Commission economists estimated that the barriers removed by the Directive raise trade and investment in services, but stressed that this is an estimate, not a measurement of what happened.

literature.citation: National Board of Trade Sweden (Kommerskollegium) (2015), Economic effects of the European Single Market: review of the empirical literature, National Board of Trade report
literature.title: Economic effects of the European Single Market: review of the empirical literature
literature.headline: No ex-post analysis of the effects of the Services Directive available at the time of the review
literature.summary_plain: A Swedish government review of the evidence found no study that had measured the Directive's actual effects.
